text.p: Queensland's slim hopes of forcing a result in their match against Sheffield Shield leaders Western Australia evaporated on Monday when key fast bowler Michael Kasprowicz suffered a knee injury.
The match petered out into a draw as Western Australia reached 320 for eight in their second innings on the final day of the four-day match at the WACA Ground in Perth.
Queensland had hoped to dismiss Western Australia cheaply to have any chance of winning the match and move out of equal third with New South Wales in the Shield standings.
Western Australia resumed on three for one wicket with an overall lead of 17 runs. Queensland's faint hopes died when former Australia bowler Kapsrowicz fell to the pitch during his 18th over.
Kaprowicz limped from the field with an injury to his right knee, casting doubt over whether he would be fit for Queensland's last two matches ahead of next month's final.
He had earlier raised Queensland's hopes by bowling number three batsman Matthew Mason for three as Western Australia slumped to 12 for two.
Number four batsman Murray Goodwin steadied the innings and went on to top-score for Western Australia with 77 while opener Ryan Campbell contributed 55.

Western Australia took two points from the match after leading on the first innings. After making 414, Western Australia dismissed Queensland for 400 to open up a six-point buffer over second-placed Tasmania in the Shield standings.
